2026 SEMA Show • 2027 Dodge Charger Gets Special-Edition Package Celebrating 90 Years of Mopar
Aston Martin Reveals the Valhalla Spider: It's Formula 1 With the Wind in Your Hair
25 photos
Photo: Aston Martin
Aston Martin has officially unveiled the Valhalla Spider. The drop-top sibling of the coupe is making its global debut at the 2026 Concours at Wynn Las Vegas as the brand' first mid-engined open-cockpit production supercar. Arriving nearly two years after the debut of the coupe, the convertible cuts off the roof while preserving design and performance specs.
It took Aston Martin ages to reveal the production Valhalla based on the AM-R 003 Concept unveiled back in March 2019 at the Geneva Motor Show. Production hurdles, redesign, and re-engineering pushed the debut date years after the original schedule. The Valhalla Coupe wasn't ready until December 2024.
Fast forward to 2026, here is the Spider version. Let's do numbers first, because that is what we are all here for, right? Long story short, the all-new Aston Martin Valhalla Spider is powered by the same flat-plane crank 4.0-liter twin-turbocharged V8, working alongside three electric motors.
While the V8 pumps out 817 horsepower (828 metric horsepower) and 627 pound-feet (850 Newton meters) of torque, the electric trio brings 247 horsepower (251 metric horsepower) and 184 pound-feet (250 Newton meters) of torque.
Photo: Aston Martin Two of the three electric motors are mounted on the front axle and power the front wheels independently, allowing the car to vary power to each front wheel to maximize cornering grip. The third electric motor sits on the rear axle, sending power exclusively to the rear wheels.
Combined, the setup puts down 1,064 horsepower (1,079 metric horsepower) and 811 pound-feet (1,100 Newton meters). That is enough to make the supercar rocket from zero to hero (0 to 60 mph or 0 to 97 kph) in just 2.4 seconds on its way to a top speed of 217 mph (350 kph), just like the coupe, despite the weight gain due to the extra reinforcement that drop-tops usually come with.
Those numbers make the Valhalla Spider the fastest open-cockpit car Aston Martin has ever built. Because yes, the brand's first mid-engined open-cockpit production supercar comes with the exact same uncompromising performance, which translates to aerodynamics, speed, and brutal acceleration metrics.
An eight-speed dual-clutch automatic transmission puts the power down through all four corners with the help of the e-AWD system. The gearbox features an integrated e-reverse function, where the electric motors handle reversing, eliminating a mechanical reverse gear to keep the gearbox lighter.
Photo: Aston Martin The Valhalla , be it a coupe or a drop-top, serves as a direct pipeline for F1-derived technology borrowed from the Aston Martin Aramco Formula 1 Team. Developed in collaboration with Aston Martin Performance Technologies (AMPT), its design focuses heavily on shaving lap times with the help of active aerodynamics, advanced materials, and motorsport ergonomics.
The core structure of the hyper-lightweight carbon fiber tub is manufactured using a combination of Resin Transfer Moulding (RTM) and F1-grade autoclave tech to keep weight under control. Furthermore, the front end sits on an F1-style pushrod suspension, featuring inboard dampers to optimize weight distribution and lower the center of gravity.
The Valhalla integrates F1-style aerodynamics. It sports wings hidden from view at the front and rear to actively modulate their angle of attack as they serve as either a Drag Reduction System (DRS) or angle upward to produce downforce. That results in 1,323 pounds (600 kilograms) of downforce at the back with the roof fitted.
In the meantime, the underfloor sports a concave surface and small slotted louvers, the so-called vortex generators, designed to act like mini diffusers and pull high-speed air out from under the car to form an incredible low-pressure ground effect.
Photo: Aston Martin The driver sits in what Aston Martin calls the "Amphitheater" interior, mimicking the cockpit of the Valkyrie hypercar. That translates to a heavily reclined seating position, also replicating the ergonomics of the Aston Martin F1 race cars driven by Fernando Alonso and Lance Stroll.
The driver gets a new carbon fiber Touring Seat, offered as standard on the Valhalla Spider for enhanced comfort and easier entry and exit. Buyers can go for the original carbon fiber seat of the coupe at no extra cost. The dihedral doors keep their ground in the convertible, now featuring a small increase in the curvature of the door glass top edge.
While the Valhalla coupe 's snorkel intake is built directly into the center of its fixed roof to supply vital cooling ducts for the intercoolers and the Hot-V turbo layout, the Spider's snorkel migrated to the rear deck spine right behind the seats, 35 millimeters higher so that it can remain fully functional even when the roof panel is removed.
When the carbon fiber roof is off, a three-piece clip-on wind deflector can be clipped directly onto the upper edge of the windshield frame to protect passengers from severe buffeting, while channeling the airflow straight back into the mid-mounted engine snorkel on the rear deck and making sure the V8 is never deprived of oxygen. The Valhalla Spider owner also goes home with a rain cover for static use.
Photo: Aston Martin Deliveries will start in the third quarter of 2027. Aston Martin hasn't revealed any pricing details just yet. The Valhalla Coupe was a $1,051,000 deal when new. The Spider is estimated to start around the $1.5 million mark.
The British firm rolled out only 999 coupes, so the Spider is also expected to be produced in low numbers to keep its exclusivity in a segment where it battles the Lamborghini Revuelto Roadster nd the Ferrari SF90 XX Spider .
